docs.title: echoChain
docs.text:
echoChain measures how an answer changes when models rewrite it in a loop. The repository is smusali/echoChain.

Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment or in .env.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install echochain

The optional baseline extra adds sentence-transformer scores:

pip install "echochain[baseline]"

docs.title: A first run
docs.text:
Dry-run from the example config:

echochain run --config examples/echochain.toml --dry-run

Run one live cycle:

echochain run --start "Redis uses epoll for I/O" --max-cycles 1 --yes

Where to go next:

  • Usage for commands, flags, configuration, output files, and exit codes.
  • Methodology for scores, conditions, analysis, and limits.
  • Contributing for the local workflow and the release process.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project uses semantic versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Subcommands run, config show, models, export, and analyze, with echochain --start kept as echochain run --start.
  • Settings from a TOML file and ECHOCHAIN_* variables, with CLI flags taking precedence.
  • Seed files with per-seed claims, selected by id with --seed.
  • Schedules alternate, swap, factorial, latin, and fixed:<model>, plus same-model, identity, and paraphrase controls.
  • --repeats for batches, and --resume to continue an interrupted run or batch.
  • A manifest.json and one JSONL row per step for every run, described by the JSON Schemas in schemas/.
  • Claim fidelity, an anchored 1 to 5 score, and a comparison with the previous answer on every answer step.
  • Judge-free length, token-survival, and generic-word metrics, plus cosine and entailment with the baseline extra.
  • echochain analyze for bootstrap curves, Kaplan-Meier survival, restricted mean time to degradation, and log-rank tests.
  • --dry-run for call, token, and cost upper bounds, with --yes required above confirm_above_usd.
  • --budget to stop a run at a USD cap with exit code 3.
  • Provider pins with order, allow_fallbacks, data_collection, and zdr.
  • --sampling-seed and top_p are sent on every call and stored on the manifest.
  • Exit codes 0, 1, 2, 3, and 130, listed in --help.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Question steps are scored for answerability and answer steps for fidelity.
  • Every chat call requires the requested parameters and disables provider fallbacks unless a pin allows them.
  • Chat calls share one HTTP client, retry transient failures, and stop at a per-call deadline.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Runs no longer write chain.csv, so use echochain export --format csv instead.
  • The backoff dependency.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• An unparsable judge reply is stored as no score instead of ending the run.
  • An empty or truncated reply is retried once instead of being recorded as an answer.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The first PyPI release, installed with pip install echochain.
  • OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the environment or .env, redacted in logs, errors, and run files.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The project is renamed from llm-telephone to echoChain.
  • Rotating models are current OpenRouter snapshots, and the judge is GPT-4.1 mini.
  • Each saved cycle records the requested model and the model that served it.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A fresh install no longer fails on a missing httpx import.
  • --help and --version work without an API key.
  • Configured model ids are checked against the OpenRouter catalog before a paid call.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv sync --group dev
uv run pytest
uv run pre-commit run --all-files

Tests call the client through an httpx2.MockTransport. A live cycle is tools/smoke.sh, and it skips when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is unset.

The documentation site uses the docs group:

uv sync --group docs && uv run mkdocs build --strict
uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
Use a short commit subject:

  • feat adds a user-visible behavior.
  • fix corrects a user-visible bug.
  • docs changes documentation only.
  • refactor changes structure without behavior.
  • test changes the suite only.
  • chore covers tooling and maintenance.

Add a model by passing --model or by changing the default tuple in src/echochain/settings.py. Add a condition in src/echochain/design.py, give it a schedule, and cover it from tests/test_design.py.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Update __version__ and docs/CHANGELOG.md.
  2. Tag vX.Y.Z on main.
  3. Publish the GitHub release. The release workflow builds the package and publishes it.
  4. The docs workflow deploys that version and points latest at it.

docs.title: Markdown
docs.text:
• Do not use an em dash, an en dash, or a spaced double hyphen.
  • Put two or more items in a bullet list, and leave one item in the sentence.
  • Keep a Mermaid label to three words and 24 characters, with no \n and no end node.
  • Write README links as absolute https://github.com/smusali/echoChain/blob/main/... URLs.
  • Keep a changelog entry to one sentence, one line, and 140 characters.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
echoChain starts from a seed answer and asks models to rewrite it. Question steps turn an answer into a question. Answer steps turn that question back into an answer. A judge scores every step, and the run stops on a rule recorded in the manifest.

flowchart LR
  Answer["Answer text"] --> Kind{"Step kind"}
  Kind -->|"question"| Ask["Answerability"]
  Kind -->|"answer"| Faith["Fidelity"]
  Faith --> Claims["Claim verdicts"]
  Ask --> Score["Numeric score"]
  Claims --> Score

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The judge scores answerability on a question step and fidelity on an answer step. Both use the prompt's 1 to 10 scale. An anchored score uses 1 to 5. When the seed lists claims, a fidelity step also records a supported or unsupported verdict for each claim. The row stores the score, the claim verdicts, and a comparison with the previous answer.

Length, token survival, and generic-word share are computed without a judge. With baseline set to off, a lexical scorer fills the comparison fields it can. With baseline set to neural, a pinned sentence-transformer model adds cosine similarity and an entailment score. A resumed run keeps the neural models recorded on its manifest.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
The rotating conditions are alternate, swap, factorial, and latin. Each one assigns the configured models to steps through a fixed schedule. fixed:<model> sends every step to one model. The controls are same-model, identity, and paraphrase. Identity uses temperature 0 and scores fidelity on every step. Paraphrase asks for a same-length rewrite. all runs the controls together with alternate.

Two models that share a vendor family cannot sit in the same rotating set. The judge panel is a separate model list. A step can call the judge more than once. The mean is missing when a reply does not parse, and the run stops if those failures exceed max_judge_error_share of the planned steps.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text: echochain analyze reads finished run directories. It writes bootstrap curves of the score by step, a Kaplan-Meier curve of steps until the score stays at or below the threshold, the restricted mean of that time, and a log-rank comparison when more than one run is given. The attractor fit regresses the last score on the first when a group has enough runs and the absolute slope is below 1.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: The score is a model judgment, not a fact check. A short chain can stop on the cycle cap before the threshold. Catalog prices can be missing, so a dry-run cost can be unknown. The lexical comparison does not measure meaning. The neural comparison depends on the pinned embedding and entailment models and is off unless requested.

docs.title: Built on
docs.text:
• Claim-level scoring, after FActScore (Min et al., EMNLP 2023).
  • The telephone chain, after Mohamed et al. (ACL 2025) and Perez et al. (ICLR 2025), whose attractor fit analyze reports.
  • Restricted mean survival time, after Royston and Parmar (BMC Medical Research Methodology, 2013).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
echoChain is a command line tool. echochain --start TEXT is the same command as echochain run --start TEXT.

flowchart TD
  Start["Start run"] --> Step["Take step"]
  Step --> Stop{"Stop rule"}
  Stop -->|"continue"| Step
  Stop -->|"threshold"| Done["Finished"]
  Stop -->|"cycles"| Done
  Stop -->|"budget"| Cap["Budget stop"]
  Stop -->|"errors"| Fail["Failed"]
  Stop -->|"interrupt"| Pause["Interrupted"]

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• run plans one cell, or a batch, and writes a run directory.
  • config show prints the resolved settings.
  • models checks the configured models against the OpenRouter catalog.
  • export RUN prints a CSV table derived from chain.jsonl.
  • analyze RUN writes tables and figures. Repeat RUN to compare runs, and pass --out DIR to choose the directory.

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text:
• --config PATH reads that TOML file instead of ./echochain.toml.
  • --quiet hides step progress.
  • --verbose prints token counts and cost with each step.
  • --help prints command help and does not need an API key.
  • --version prints the package version and does not need an API key.

docs.title: Run flags
docs.text:
• --start TEXT is the inline seed text.
  • --seed ID selects one seed from the seed file.
  • --seeds PATH reads a seed file. With no --seed, every seed in that file runs.
  • --condition NAME chooses a schedule. Repeat the flag to run several.
  • --repeats N repeats each seed and condition pair.
  • --sampling-seed N sets the base sampling seed.
  • --top-p N sets the nucleus sampling cutoff.
  • --dry-run prints call, token, and cost upper bounds and does not call a model.
  • --yes starts a run whose dry-run cost is above confirm_above_usd.
  • --out DIR is the directory that receives run folders.
  • --budget USD stops the run at that cost.
  • --model ID adds a rotating model. Repeat the flag to replace the default list.
  • --judge ID adds a judge model. Repeat the flag to replace the default judge.
  • --judge-samples N is the number of judge samples per step.
  • --judge-temperature N is the judge temperature.
  • --temperature N is the transform temperature.
  • --max-cycles N is the number of planned steps.
  • --max-tokens N is the completion token cap.
  • --stop-score N is the low fidelity threshold.
  • --stop-consecutive N is how many low scores stop a run. Zero means the threshold never stops the run.
  • --provider SPEC pins a model to providers, as model=provider,provider|true.
  • --resume ID continues a run id, a run directory, or a batch id.

--start cannot be combined with --seed or --seeds. A run with none of the three selectors is an error. --seed with no --seeds reads the packaged seed file. --resume cannot be combined with a new selector or with --dry-run.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Settings resolve in this order:

  1. Built-in defaults.
  2. echochain.toml in the working directory, or the file from --config.
  3. Environment variables.
  4. CLI flags.

These settings have no flag:

  • base_url (OPENROUTER_API_BASE) is the OpenRouter API root.
  • deadline_seconds (ECHOCHAIN_DEADLINE_SECONDS) is the per-call deadline.
  • confirm_above_usd (ECHOCHAIN_CONFIRM_ABOVE) asks for --yes above this dry-run cost.
  • http_referer (ECHOCHAIN_HTTP_REFERER) and title (ECHOCHAIN_TITLE) are request headers.
  • baseline (ECHOCHAIN_BASELINE) is off or neural. The default is off.
  • max_judge_error_share (ECHOCHAIN_MAX_JUDGE_ERROR_SHARE) stops the run when judge failures exceed this share of the planned steps. The default is 0.1.

A TOML provider pin can also set data_collection to allow or deny, and zdr to true or false:

[providers."openai/gpt-4.1-mini"]
order = ["openai"]
allow_fallbacks = false
data_collection = "deny"
zdr = true

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Each run is a directory under --out. The directory name is a UTC timestamp and a random id. The manifest stores a short slug, the seed text, the claims, and the rules used for that run.

  • manifest.json is the run record, including version, seed_text, claims, and max_judge_error_share.
  • chain.jsonl has one JSON object per step, including input_text, output_text, and sampling_seed.
  • BATCH.batch.json stores the settings for a multi-cell run.
  • echochain analyze writes curves.tsv, survival.tsv, comparisons.tsv, curves.svg, and survival.svg.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 means the cycle cap or the fidelity threshold was reached.
  • 1 means a runtime or API failure, including a generation error or a judge error.
  • 2 means a usage or configuration error.
  • 3 means the budget was exceeded or the account is out of credits.
  • 130 means the process was interrupted.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: --dry-run estimates calls, prompt tokens, and USD from catalog prices. When the estimate is above confirm_above_usd, the run waits for --yes. --budget stops a live run at a USD cap and exits 3. A missing price makes the bound unknown.

docs.title: Resume
docs.text: --resume rebuilds the run from manifest.json. It does not reread the seed file. The stored seed text, claims, models, temperatures, stop rule, and sampling seed stay in force. Client settings such as the API root and provider pins come from the current process. A manifest that recorded neural baseline models keeps those models. A run with no completed step resumes at step 1. An interrupted batch cell resumes from its own manifest, and a cell that never started uses the batch file.

docs.title: Data handling
docs.text: Prompts and model replies are sent to OpenRouter and then to the selected providers. The API key is read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY or .env and redacted in logs, errors, and run files. Run files store the seed, the prompts' visible text, and the replies on disk under --out. Provider pins can set data_collection and zdr for a model. Fallbacks stay off unless a pin sets allow_fallbacks to true.
